text: Swimming is an old discipline where kicking comes before breathing. The motion demands that back muscles, notably the quadriceps and hamstrings, stabilize the body and drive it forward. This action keeps the center of gravity aligned with the current, thereby maximizing speed and reducing trapped air. Subsequently, breathing occurs, a process reliant on abdominal engagement, specifically the diaphragm contracting to expand lung volume and draw in oxygen. The swimmer must perpetually juggle these two functions, demanding precise coordination and the readiness to expend stored energy in order to move efficiently and enjoyably.
